chunks: And Pharaoh called out to his people, saying: 'O my people, is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?'
ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh claim about his dominion and the rivers of Egypt?
ai.summary: In Surah Az-Zukhruf, Pharaoh’s rhetorical question underscores his arrogance by equating his political dominion over Egypt’s Nile rivers with divine authority, a theme central to the Surah’s critique of polytheism. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, note that this boast reflects the tyrant’s delusion that material control equates to ultimate sovereignty, contrasting sharply with the monotheistic view of God as the true source of all blessings.
